summary: Final review of the 5-cycle dogfood-driven PDCA campaign (Cycles 11-15): a plan-vs-research ADEQUACY critic (was planning balanced against evidence?), a COMPLETENESS critic (what is still missing/weakest?), and a REGRESSION/consistency sweep (do the claims match the repo state?).
logs: campaign review: adequacy=sound · completeness=lean / a-few-real-gaps (near diminishing returns — consolidate, don't keep adding gates) · regression=clean | findings 13 (high 1)

verdicts.completeness: lean / a-few-real-gaps (near diminishing returns — consolidate, don't keep adding gates)

high_findings.point: Self-inconsistency / trust regression: the skill's own dogfood output (eval/dogfood-cbdc-2026-06-29.md), preserved as Cycle 11 evidence, now FAILS its own gate — it ends [FINAL]: VALID with [FALSIFY]=PASS and [NULL]=NA but carries no [SKEPTIC] line, which Cycle 12 made mandatory. `python scripts/compliance_check.py eval/dogfood-cbdc-2026-06-29.md` exits 1. The canonical worked example a reader would copy is now non-compliant. This is the clearest 'what real use hits next': anyone dogfooding or pattern-matching off this file ships a gate-failing report. Fix is one line (add [SKEPTIC]=PASS) but it signals nobody re-runs the preserved artifacts after a gate change.

all_findings.point: Cycle 11 and 12 are strongly grounded and self-corrected: the dogfood cuts map directly onto the fixes, and both in-cycle defects (Cycle 11's 6 highs; Cycle 12's NULL=PASS skeptic-bypass) were caught by run-confirming verification subagents, not merely claimed. Verified live: eval 13/13 / FP 0/3, the §8 symmetric check and bad-null-dodge fixture are present in HEAD.

No cycle was over-engineered or solved a non-problem. The trust cuts honored the Cycle-2 lesson (structural token checks, substance left to the author!=reviewer judge) instead of building brittle semantic regex gates; the doc cuts (13-15) stayed minimal. This is the correct plan/research balance, not gold-plating.

Cycle 12 shipped behind a real loophole that the FIRST verification pass caught (the NULL=PASS dodge was a pre-existing asymmetry, not introduced by §9, but Cycle 12 newly made it a one-token bypass of the whole cycle). The loop closed it in-cycle, but it shows the original Cycle-12 plan under-scoped the exemption surface — a near-miss that depended on the red-team rather than the plan.

Cycles 13, 14, 15 carry no adversarial red-team and only inline/self-check verification ('no red-team warranted; ponytail'). Defensible for doc-only/trivial-helper changes, but Cycle 15's primary-over-secondary rule and Cycle 14's lite-mode trigger are discipline cues with no fixture or test pinning them, so regressions to that guidance would go unnoticed by the gate.

Two LOW pre-existing parser quirks (annotated '[PASS — note]' verdicts read as non-PASS; a '[GATE]:' prose line outside the fence overwriting a verdict) were surfaced by the Cycle-12 red-team and deferred to the backlog rather than fixed. Correctly triaged as unreachable by template-following output and affecting all gates, but they remain open debt across the gate, not just one cycle.

Documented residual boundaries are honest but real: a plain-200 soft-404 with no redirect still reads 'live' (status-only probe limit) and a suspect-only --check-links run still reports effective:true. These are surfaced in IMPROVEMENT.md and reassigned to the skeptic-judge rather than hidden, which is the right call, but they cap how much trust --check-links actually adds.

Self-inconsistency / trust regression: the skill's own dogfood output (eval/dogfood-cbdc-2026-06-29.md), preserved as Cycle 11 evidence, now FAILS its own gate — it ends [FINAL]: VALID with [FALSIFY]=PASS and [NULL]=NA but carries no [SKEPTIC] line, which Cycle 12 made mandatory. `python scripts/compliance_check.py eval/dogfood-cbdc-2026-06-29.md` exits 1. The canonical worked example a reader would copy is now non-compliant. This is the clearest 'what real use hits next': anyone dogfooding or pattern-matching off this file ships a gate-failing report. Fix is one line (add [SKEPTIC]=PASS) but it signals nobody re-runs the preserved artifacts after a gate change.

[L2] vault-integration is a declared compliance gate ([L2]: Vault/dedup path considered) yet has zero implementation: no knowledge/00_inbox path, no template, no script, no fixture testing it. It is pure honor-system prose that the deterministic gate cannot verify, so [L2]=PASS means nothing — every report just asserts it. Either make it actionable (a real inbox-write/dedup step or helper) or demote it from a PASS-required gate to a note. As-is it dilutes the credibility of the 'validator-as-gate, not honor-system' claim that the whole skill rests on.

The handoff mechanism is documented prominently in SKILL.md (write .claude/handoffs/handoff-<ts>.json, resume by reading it) but there is no template, no helper, no example, and no .claude/handoffs dir — it is described capability with no scaffolding. A plan→execute session split (a real multi-session research use) would land here with nothing to follow. Either add a tiny handoff template/snippet (mirroring framed-question.template.md) or trim the claim. Low-reach but it is the one documented workflow with zero support.

Deferred parser quirks (logged in IMPROVEMENT.md, confirmed live): gate-line parsing is NOT scoped to the fenced compliance block — compliance_check.py scans the whole document for ^[GATE]: lines, so a stray [GATE]: line in prose outside the fence can overwrite a recorded verdict, and an annotated verdict like [PASS — note] is read as non-PASS (the last-bracket rule). Both are reachable by an unusual-but-honest report (e.g. an author who annotates a verdict). Genuinely low-severity since a template-following report avoids them, but they are latent false-positive/bypass surfaces in the one piece of code everything trusts. A single normalization pass (scope to fence + first-token verdict) closes both.

Link-liveness (--check-links) has an acknowledged blind spot the team itself flagged as a residual boundary: a plain-200 soft-404 with no redirect still reads 'live'. This is correctly assigned to the skeptic-judge's semantic job rather than the probe, so it is documented-not-fixed, which is the right call. Noting it only so it is not mistaken for a closed gap — it is the realistic next thing a dead-but-200 source would slip through, and it is bounded, not a defect to chase.

Usability/onboarding: there is no end-to-end worked example that PASSES the current gate. The dogfood (now failing) was the de-facto example; good-positive is a terse fixture, not a teaching artifact. A first-time user has the templates and the directive but no single 'here is a complete real report that exits 0' reference. Minor, but it is the gap between a correct skill and an easily-adopted one.

Minor stale prose count in IMPROVEMENT.md Cycle 11 FIX paragraph (line 219): it states the unit test classifies 'unverified 6', but the actual test (tests/test_check_links.py) and live run report unverified=7. This is internally consistent with the SAME cycle's ACT note (line 224), which adds the EAI_AGAIN→unverified case ('the unit test covers EAI_NONAME→nxdomain vs EAI_AGAIN→unverified'), bumping unverified 6→7. So the FIX-stage snapshot (6) is a pre-ACT figure that was not updated after the in-cycle EAI_AGAIN addition. The authoritative artifact (the green test) is correct; only the narrative count is one behind.

reports.summary: All five cycles (11-15) trace to a single real dogfood run (eval/dogfood-cbdc-2026-06-29.md): the gate claimed "[L1] verified live" while verifying nothing (Cycle 11), the skeptic verdict floated free of the gated artifact (Cycle 12), sources were hand-stamped (Cycle 13), framing was heavy for a one-fact query (Cycle 14), and a law-firm blog was cited for an executive order instead of the Federal Register primary (Cycle 15) — each cut is visible in the actual artifact, not invented. Planning was well balanced against research: trust-bearing changes (11, 12) got code + frozen fixtures + 3-4 independent run-confirming subagents, while the ergonomic/doc cuts (13, 14, 15) were correctly kept lightweight per the "ponytail" shortest-diff rule rather than over-engineered. Critically, the headline in-cycle catches were genuinely caught by verification, not asserted: I independently confirmed Cycle 11's 6 highs are closed (eval 13/13, the _is_nxdomain EAI_NONAME fix is in the code) and Cycle 12's NULL=PASS dodge was run-confirmed live by two separate red-team lenses (exit 0 on the dodge) and is now closed by the symmetric §8 check at lines 136-137 plus the bad-null-dodge fixture. The loop demonstrably stopped brittle/incomplete first cuts from shipping — exactly its purpose.
reports.recommendation: Ship/keep all five cycles — the campaign is sound and evidence-grounded. To raise it from sound to airtight: (1) Treat the Cycle-12 near-miss as a process signal — when a new gate adds an EXEMPTION (null/HTML/INVALID), the plan should pre-enumerate the symmetric forge path before DO, so the red-team confirms rather than discovers it. (2) Add at least the cheap exemption-boundary fixture the adequacy critic flagged (good-negative must keep passing without [SKEPTIC]) so future §9 hardening can't silently false-positive honest null reports. (3) Pin Cycle 14/15 discipline cues with a lightweight check or example fixture if they ever regress in practice. (4) Schedule the two deferred parser quirks (first-token normalization + scope parsing to the fence) as a single small uniform hardening cycle before they bite a real output. No cycle needs reverting.

reports.verdict: lean / a-few-real-gaps (near diminishing returns — consolidate, don't keep adding gates)
reports.summary: After Cycles 11-15 the skill is mature and well-disciplined: a deterministic compliance gate (16 fixtures, detection 1.0 / FP 0), a semantic skeptic-judge, opt-in link-liveness, HTML self-containment, CI, and a tight PDCA log. Coverage (10 source domains), trust (per-claim corroboration, primary-over-secondary, skeptic binding), and robustness (red-teamed gates) are all strong. The genuine remaining gaps are narrow and mostly about loose ends that earlier cycles created or left unfinished — not missing capability. The single most telling one: the skill's own dogfood artifact now FAILS its own gate, because Cycle 12 added [SKEPTIC] but nobody back-filled the dogfood. Two declared gates ([L2] vault, the handoff mechanism) are prose-only with no implementation, so they are honor-system checks the deterministic gate can't actually enforce. The deferred parser quirks are real but low-reach. I recommend consolidating (fix the self-inconsistency, decide whether [L2]/handoff are real or should be demoted) and then stopping the add-a-gate loop — further deterministic checks risk gold-plating and Cycle-2-style brittleness.
reports.recommendation: Consolidate, then stop the add-a-gate loop — the skill is at diminishing returns on new checks. Do a short cleanup cycle, not more capability: (1) HIGH — back-fill [SKEPTIC]=PASS into eval/dogfood-cbdc-2026-06-29.md so the canonical example passes its own gate, and add a one-line CHECK step to the PDCA loop that re-runs the gate over preserved artifacts after any gate change (prevents this class of regression). (2) MED — resolve the two prose-only gates honestly: either give [L2] and the handoff real scaffolding (a tiny helper/template + one fixture each) or demote them from PASS-required gates to documented notes, so every deterministic gate is actually enforceable. (3) LOW/optional — fold the deferred parser normalization (fence-scope + first-token verdict) into the same cleanup since it touches the trusted code path. Do NOT add new failure-mode gates, new source domains, or new output formats unless a real run demands them — that would be gold-plating and risks Cycle-2-style brittleness. After the cleanup cycle, declare the skill stable and switch the loop from 'improve' to 'maintain' (run on real questions; only reopen when a genuine dogfood cut appears).
